note_tweet.text:
Typing to your agent is so 2025. Here are three dictation apps built with Voz, so you can talk instead.

∗ Takt puts push-to-talk on Windows: hold Right Alt, talk, and the text lands in whatever app you’re in. Clear cleans up the mic audio first.

∗ Whisper Anywhere does voice typing from the Windows tray, with Voz as the default, and never writes a recording to disk.

∗ OpenFlow brings it to Android as a floating bubble that shows up with the keyboard, with Ear detecting the language.

Every word is transcribed on device. Links in the thread.

note_tweet.text:
A cloud API call doesn’t need your contacts’ names.

Cue, @AgrawalHridaya’s smart clipboard for Mac, strips them out before anything leaves your machine. Redact runs on the device and swaps names, phone numbers and addresses for placeholders, so the cloud model sees [GIVEN_NAME_1], not Maya.

The paste still uses your real text, and if Redact can’t run, Cue does a plain paste instead of sending anything unredacted.

Very cool.

https://t.co/OvlxaSiY9x

note_tweet.text:
WhisperX uses a 378MB model to time English words.

Align does it in 0.7MB.

Give it any transcript and it corrects each word’s start and end time against the audio, so captions highlight every word exactly as it’s spoken.

On 258 word boundaries checked by hand, Align was off by 45ms on average. WhisperX was off by 53.5ms.
